why: A BN4 Navi chip whose Navi is moved (a unit of kind navi, tools/xchiprecipe_bn4_navi.py; src/emu/xchips_bn4.c's XCHIP_NAVI rows) runs in BN6's engine as BN6's Navi chips do, and is read so. Its family: BN4 runs its Navi chips by its support state (MegaMan's state 0x0C, 0x080EB9EA: the chip's routine of the table 0x080220E0 by its subfamily, then the attack's end in the same frame), BN6 by a family of their own, 0x1B (0x080ED690: its Navi chip object's spawner 0x080E2C6C with the subfamily in r3, the same registers handed on, then the attack's end in the same frame, where its support family 0x15 holds MegaMan a frame more: megaman_clock). The chip's registry row is XREG_MOVED and names a BN6 Navi chip as the twin whose family its record takes (src/core/xchips_record.c xrec_from_bn4; BN6's Roll, 221), its subfamily the unit's number in BN6's grown Navi routines. So where the chip in MegaMan's AI data (chip_id's place) is such a row's, BN4's state 0x0C is read as that twin's record's family, read from BN6's ROM. Its object: BN4's routine spawns a fourth-kind object of the Navi's own (GutsMan's type 0x10, 0x080E31E8), BN6's spawner its one Navi chip object (type 0x10, 0x080E2B28), the same four states (tools/xchiprecipe_bn4_navi.py OBJECTS, each BN4 object read against BN6's): BN4's object, found as the type the unit's routine of BN4's support table spawns (the common spawner's shape, support_objects), is read as BN6's type 0x10; its element at BN6's +0x0E (BN4's spawner stores r3 at +0x17, BN6's at +0x0E); the spawn's leftover r3 at +0x3C, BN4's routine's own address (the support run's bx r3) and BN6's the subfamily (0x080ED696: ldrb r3,[r7,#3]), as the unit's number, and BN6's copy of it at +0x19 (0x080E2C98-0x080E2C9A: ldr r1,[r0,#0x3c]; strb r1,[r0,#0x19]), which no code of BN4's object reads or writes; and the chip at +0x30 as the run's id. Not a mask: an object of another type, or one whose +0x3C is not its routine's address, is compared as it is.
evidence: bn4_chip_gutsman t32: MegaMan's CurAction BN4 0x0C, BN6 0x1B, the frame the chip is used in both
bn4_chip_gutsman t33: the object's +0x19 0 and 0x85, +0x3C 0x080E3305 (BN4's routine) and 0x85
